title: Sieve and riddle making returns from extinction
subject: Public evidence about how UK sieve and riddle making moved from a reported last maker and later extinction classification into renewed practice, and what remains unknown about the actual transmission of tacit skill.

living_practice_status.boundary: These are Heritage Crafts' published research claims on a page naming the 2025 Red List review cycle. The 2026 check date is a source-read date, not a new census. The Human Record did not independently count practitioners or adjudicate craft viability.

selection.chosen_by: Framework under COM #347 after a bounded at-risk knowledge/creativity quarry and strongest-owner subtraction.
selection.basis: The case contains a visible public transition from reported last maker, through an extinction classification, into revival and new training. It tests transmission-lineage recording without treating documentation as preservation of a living skill.
selection.strongest_owner: Heritage Crafts for current UK craft status, viability, practitioners, training routes and safeguarding.
selection.thr_gap: Preserve the public source ancestry of the revival story, separate attention pathways from skill transmission, and keep the missing parts of the tacit-knowledge chain visible.
not_implied: that this craft is more culturally important than other endangered practices
that The Human Record can preserve the craft itself
that named practitioners endorse or participate in this record
that a public process description substitutes for direct teaching or practice
selection.stop_or_shrink_condition: If a stronger owner preserves the transmission lineage more completely and accessibly, link outward and reduce or retire duplicative THR material.

nodes.title: How to make a sieve and riddle
nodes.role: Contemporary reporting from Mike Turnock's workshop. Reports that, as far as Turnock knew, he was the last British handmade sieve-and-riddle maker; records family/business continuity and his hope to find someone to train before retirement.
nodes.boundary: Independent reporting about Turnock is not independent proof that no other maker existed in the UK. Detailed process text and images are not reproduced by this record.

nodes.title: Craft skills under threat with 37 additions to the Red List of Endangered Crafts
nodes.role: Reports that sieve and riddle making had been listed extinct in the 2017 Red List and had been revived by two new makers who were beginning commercial production by March 2019.
nodes.boundary: Same institutional source family as the current Heritage Crafts craft entry; separate URLs are not independent witnesses.

nodes.title: Sieve and riddle making
nodes.review_cycle: 2025 Red List reviewers named on page
nodes.role: Current craft-status owner used by this record. Reports critically endangered status; 0 main-income professionals, 1 side-income professional, 1 trainee; says Mike Turnock retired in 2010 and the craft was extinct until 2018; identifies Steve Overthrow and Colin Davies as current makers and describes public-attention pathways into the craft.
nodes.boundary: The Human Record defers current status and practitioner-count claims to Heritage Crafts rather than independently verifying them.

nodes.title: The HCA Red List of Endangered Crafts — 2019 edition
nodes.role: The 2019 Red List entry reports that Steve Overthrow began making at the beginning of 2018, received advice and tuition from Mike Turnock, and also went through product development and refining before commercial production; the report does not establish a strict sequence between those learning components.
nodes.boundary: Same institutional evidence family as the Heritage Crafts announcement/current page. This records reported learning-route components, not the exact teaching content, completeness of transmission or independent observation of tuition.

nodes.title: Steve Overthrow
nodes.role: Overthrow reports learning partly from Mike Turnock and receiving knowledge he could not find through research.
nodes.boundary: Published first-person account, not independent verification or a THR interview. Interview and teaching dates are not established. Does not establish exact teaching content, completeness, or Colin Davies's learning route.

nodes.title: Sieves and riddles: discover the company making handmade garden sieves
nodes.role: Published interview reports that Overthrow began researching the extinct craft, learned through repeated trial and error while developing his making practice, and also received Turnock's advice/help on aspects he said he could not have researched. Exact sequence and overlap are not fully established by the record.
nodes.boundary: Published practitioner account, not a THR interview or independent observation of learning. This record preserves learning modes only and does not reproduce practitioner-specific process instructions.

nodes.title: Sieve and riddle maker website / process page
nodes.role: Heritage Crafts says the practitioner website contains details of the sieve-making process.
nodes.boundary: The current research aperture did not obtain the linked site/process page. One fetch returned a 502 and another was unavailable from cache. FETCH_FAILED_HERE != SITE_GONE. No finding depends on unseen content.

lineage_events.event: Guardian reports Mike Turnock as, to his knowledge, the last British handmade sieve-and-riddle maker and records his wish to find a successor before retirement.
Heritage Crafts currently reports that Mike Turnock retired in 2010.
Heritage Crafts reports that sieve and riddle making was listed extinct in the first Red List.
The current Heritage Crafts page describes the extinction interval as lasting until 2018.

Public Heritage Crafts and practitioner-interview sources report components of Overthrow's learning route including research, trial-and-error/product development, and advice or tuition from Mike Turnock; exact sequence, overlap and relative contribution remain unresolved.
Heritage Crafts reports two new makers had revived the craft and were beginning commercial production.

Heritage Crafts identifies Steve Overthrow and Colin Davies in the revival/current-practice record, reports Steve is focusing on training a new maker, and classifies the craft as critically endangered.

current_findings: A 2009 independent newspaper feature recorded Mike Turnock as, to his knowledge, the last British handmade sieve-and-riddle maker and documented his intention to retire if he could find a successor.
Heritage Crafts reports that the craft was listed extinct in 2017 and had been revived by two new makers by March 2019.
Heritage Crafts currently identifies Steve Overthrow's discovery of the Red List and Colin Davies's viewing of a Countryfile feature as pathways into making.
Heritage Crafts currently classifies the practice as critically endangered rather than extinct.

The Red List and media pathways establish attention, not skill transmission by themselves. For Overthrow specifically, later public sources report a mixed learning route involving research, trial-and-error/product development, and direct advice or tuition from Mike Turnock.

Across the published accounts, Overthrow reports receiving knowledge from Turnock that he could not obtain through research. This narrows the transmission gap but does not establish the exact teaching content, relative contribution of each learning route, or completeness of tacit-knowledge survival.
unknowns: What was transmitted, what was reconstructed or newly learned, and through which routes.
Exactly what knowledge passed through the Turnock-to-Overthrow learning route reported in the Homo Faber interview, and what other transmission occurred.

For Overthrow, public sources now identify research, trial-and-error/product development and Turnock advice/tuition as reported components, but their timing, relative contribution, exact tacit content and completeness remain unresolved.
For Colin Davies, the learning route beyond the reported Countryfile/Red List attention pathway remains unresolved in this record.
Which parts of the older Hill & Sons practice survive unchanged and which have been adapted.
Whether all materially important tacit knowledge survived the extinction interval.
The identity or training stage of the current trainee beyond Heritage Crafts' aggregate count.
The completeness of the current practitioner count.
The current general availability and contents of the practitioner process website linked by Heritage Crafts.
not_checked: Interviews conducted by THR with Mike Turnock, Steve Overthrow, Colin Davies or the current trainee; the published Homo Faber interview with Overthrow was checked.
The BBC Countryfile episode described by Heritage Crafts.
Steve Overthrow's process website content, because it was not retrieved in this research aperture.
Surviving Hill & Sons tools, patterns, workshop records or business archives.
Physical comparison of work from different generations.
Independent search for practitioners outside the Heritage Crafts count.

source_independence.warning: The Heritage Crafts announcement, 2019 Red List report and current craft page are separate publications but one institutional evidence family. The current Heritage Crafts page also cites the Guardian feature. Homo Faber and Gardens Illustrated are separate publishers, but both carry practitioner-reported learning accounts; distinct publications are not automatically independent witnesses to the underlying teaching. The practitioner site was not inspected and is not evidence for current findings.

corrections.basis: Heritage Crafts 2019 Red List report + Gardens Illustrated 2023 published practitioner interview
corrections.change: Narrowed the Overthrow transmission gap from a generic direct-learning route to reported components: research, trial-and-error/product development, and Turnock advice/tuition. Exact sequence/overlap, tacit content, timing, relative contribution and completeness remain unknown; no process manual or practitioner contact was added.

corrections.discovery_credit: Dola's ELITISM lead, relayed by Mark, led Codex to the published Homo Faber interview. No independent corroboration between the publications is claimed.
corrections.change: Added Overthrow's published account of learning partly from Turnock. Precise content, dates and completeness remain unknown.
Made reconstruction/new learning explicit alternatives to transmission, recorded a known cross-publisher citation, and separated source-read date from review cycle.

authority_and_consent.strongest_owner: Heritage Crafts for current UK craft status and safeguarding.
authority_and_consent.public_source_scope: This case summarizes already-public reporting about named practitioners and source relationships.
authority_and_consent.future_boundary: Any practitioner-specific recording of tacit knowledge, workshop practice, tools, voice, video or teaching requires a separate permission/authority decision. Cultural risk is not permission to extract.

correction_rule: Bring stronger public evidence about the transmission chain, dates, source relationships or current-status boundaries. Do not submit private practitioner information or unpublished process material without the right to share it.
invariants: REPORTED LEARNING MODES != COMPLETE SKILL-TRANSFER RECONSTRUCTION
